segments.text: Country road. Sunny afternoon. Just a little breeze.
Then the breeze becomes a tornado. It takes the car in front of you. And spins it, right above your head. What do you do?
Most drivers think: floor it, and get out of here.
Big mistake. Tornadoes love fast cars. It turns around, and sucks you up too.
Now you're spinning with the red car, a cow, a caravan, and a garden gnome. Until it spits you out. Right onto a windmill. And you're still spinning.
Here's how you do it properly.
Pull over into the field. The tornado spins one way. So you drive in circles, the other way.
Round and round. Faster and faster.
The tornado gets dizzy. It wobbles. And it gently puts the red car back down. Right side up.
Then it shrinks into a tiny breeze, and blows the dust off your car.
And from above? Your tyre tracks are the best crop circle in the country.
Next exam question: the drawbridge opens, with you on it. Follow, so you don't miss it.
